data.body: Operator 2026-10-19: research graph engineering for AI agents; where does it help ddflow, and file the phase if useful. Research (three reports, /tmp/claude-1001/research/graph-landscape.md, graph-internal.md, graph-codegraph.md; committed copies via DX-commit-research-reports): ddflow is already the graph (event log + needs + leases + gates); the scheduling graphs are cheap (plan 0.12 s, critical_path 0.02 s, waves 0.63 s on 2735 items; ddflow next is 2.6 s of which 1.7 s is reading and folding the 65 MB log, so B-perf-mcp-start matters more than any graph cache). Worth building: (1) ONE effective edge set on State (six+ bugs came from readiness, critical_path, progress and the restamp scripts each re-deriving it: B27, B67, B79c2f6e17a, B13ed484062, Bbbcbfc4bbb, B43447abfc8); (2) a persisted import graph (testreach.build re-parses 1487 files in 5.6 s on every selection) keyed by blob hash; (3) one impact query that P-context-sync.impact, .prompt, .conflict, PD-baseline, CN-consumers and B-dec-monitor each otherwise reimplement; (4) wave/depth as a derived attribute instead of hand-stamped wave:N tags; (5) impact-aware review scope. DELIBERATELY NOT built (revisit only with evidence): GraphRAG or knowledge-graph agent memory (ICLR 2026 study: frequently underperforms vanilla RAG; Zep gains 1.4 points on DMR, vendor-measured), SCIP/CodeQL/Sourcegraph indexers (external dependencies, D-graph-stdlib), full reverse-import closure for test selection (median module reaches 459 of 810 tests, core/records.py 92%), incremental ready/wave maintenance (saves ~0.1 s), a unified typed property graph over items+records+files+symbols, decision relevance by graph distance. Policy D-graph-stdlib stands: stdlib graphlib plus core/graph; networkx only as a dev-only test oracle. Extend core/graph and services/testreach.py; do not add a second graph engine. Success is measured, not argued: GR-acceptance.
data.title: Graph foundations: one effective edge set, a cached import graph, impact queries; stdlib only, no new subsystem

data.body:
Operator 2026-09-28: 'after a merge of the work of few subagents the whole code should be tested for compilation, bugging, code quality and full suite test'. Today merge() lands one item at a time (api/lifecycle.py:499-624) and every item runs its own full unit_tests/bug_hunt/dedupe; the phase close is the only combined check and fires only when a whole phase is done. (a) an 'integration' gate set ([gates] integration_pipeline: build/import check, standards, unit_tests full, bug_hunt over the combined diff) run after N merges or on demand ('ddflow integrate'); (b) 'merge --batch A,B,C' lands several independent branches onto an integration ref, runs the integration pipeline once, and fast-forwards the base only if green — a red batch is bisected to the item that broke it (reuse B26's bisect idea); (c) per-item unit_tests may then be the selected subset (B16) because the batch runs the full suite; (d) the integration result is recorded against every item in the batch. Test: a batch whose second item breaks a test does not reach the base, and the culprit is named.

NOTE 2026-10-19 (graph phase P-graph): merge-queue ordering by needs and glob overlap among queued items (audit candidate M) belongs here; use ItemGraph (GR-itemgraph), do not add a second edge derivation.

Research reports written 2026-10-16..19 live only in /tmp/claude-1001/research/ (not durable): coderabbit.md, deep-research.md, history-collapse-extract.md, openhands.md, devin.md, codegen-clickup.md, orphan-recovery.md, config-external.md, config-internal.md, plan-modes.md, sdd.md, graph-landscape.md (+ graph-internal.md, graph-codegraph.md when done). Copy them to docs/ddflow/research/ (strip secrets, check sizes), then repoint every task body that cites a /tmp/claude-1001/research path (ddflow search 'claude-1001/research') with ddflow update --append-body or the shipped edit verb. Do not rewrite the reports.

ALSO commit graph-landscape.md, graph-internal.md, graph-codegraph.md and graph_probe.py (the probe script, no private data); the P-graph phase body cites them.

Today readiness (core/schedule.py plan), critical_path (:984), progress._waits_on, plancheck.reaches and the restamp scripts each derive 'effective dependencies' separately, and four places scan for reverse edges (api/rename.py:21 _dependents, core/stuck.py:35, services/waiting.py:125 waiters, plancheck). Add a lazy, cached-per-fold ItemGraph on State (like _child_index): needs, inherited_needs (through ancestors), dependents(id), children, depth(id), and the effective edge set the scheduler uses, all computed once through core/graph (stdlib). Tests: parity with the current plan/critical_path outputs on the real log and on random DAGs (B-par-equivalence-tests), compared against networkx as a dev-only oracle; one regression test per old bug class (B27, B67, B43447abfc8). No behaviour change in this task: only the single definition and its accessors. Measure: ItemGraph build adds under 50 ms on 2735 items. Conformance: D-graph-stdlib, r-reuse-core, files under 20 KB.
data.title: One ItemGraph view on State: needs, inherited needs, dependents, children, depth, effective scheduling edges

data.body: services/testreach.py:build parses 1487 files with ast on EVERY ddflow tests / testselect / testscope call: 5.6 s cold (4.3 s in the probe), 119 KB pickled. Cache per-file imports (and facade exports/uses) in the git-ignored .ddflow/cache/importgraph.json keyed by git blob hash (git ls-files -s; tree-hash fast path when nothing changed), re-parse only changed blobs, invalidate on a schema version, never trust a cache entry whose blob hash differs; a corrupt or missing cache falls back to a full build (unavailable is never a silent empty graph). Reused across the ci and unit_tests gates of one item. Regression: selection output is byte-identical with and without the cache on the last 50 merges; warm build measured under 1 s (report cold, warm, and the speedup). Stdlib only (json, hashlib via ddflow.core.digest, fsio for atomic writes: the architecture guards forbid raw tempfile/fcntl/hashlib). Feeds GR-graph-blast, GR-reach-recall, GR-impact-query.
data.title: Persist the Python import graph per file by blob hash; warm build under a second

data.body: Replace the ad hoc edge derivations and the four reverse-edge scans with ItemGraph (GR-itemgraph). Behaviour-preserving: the full existing scheduler/progress/rename suites stay green, plus a differential test that old and new agree on the real event log for next/ready/blocked/critical_path/progress. Close the bug class: a new test fails if a module re-derives inherited needs itself (ratchet). Conformance: small files, no new runtime dependency.

data.body: Replay of 10 merges (graph-codegraph.md): the existing selector reached 9.5% of tests with recall 0.92 (misses at 0.50 and 0.67), full reverse closure reached 71% with recall 1.00 (median module reaches 459 of 810 tests, so closure is useless). 33 files use importlib/__import__, and registry-by-convention, subprocess CLI tests and data files are invisible to imports. Extend the recall replay (tests/test_testselect_recall.py) to the last 200 merges and every real CI failure in the log, then tune hop cap and hub cut-off and add widening rules (a changed dynamic-import or registry file widens to its registry's tests; changed data files map to their readers) until recall >= 0.98 at <= 15% of tests, reporting precision/recall per setting; keep the always-run guards (DX-ci-always-run-guards) and the full suite in the merge queue. Never lower recall to gain speed: report the trade table.
data.title: Tune test reach against real misses: hop cap, hub cut, dynamic-import and registry widening

data.body: A read-only command (CLI + MCP declared command, matrix parity) answering what a file change reaches: modules by hop, tests selected (and why: import, name, conftest, GOVERNS, data file), and the full-closure size for comparison. Uses the cached import graph. Human and --json output; exit codes 0/2. Useful for agents choosing selective tests and for operators sizing a hot-file change (core/records.py reaches 747 of 810 tests, api/review.py 452).
data.title: ddflow graph blast <path>: the modules and tests a change reaches, with the hop budget

data.body: Many open tasks need 'what does this change affect' and would each write their own: P-context-sync.impact, .prompt and .conflict, PD-baseline, CN-consumers, B-dec-monitor, B-cochange-*. Build it once: given files or a record id, return open leases and items whose globs overlap or whose needs transit (ItemGraph), decisions/rules/lessons whose globs govern the files, and the tests reached (cached import graph). Typed result with the reason per edge, bounded size, deterministic order; CLI + MCP parity. P-context-sync.impact becomes a consumer of this and is not to re-implement the walk.
data.title: One impact query: what a file, rule, decision or lesson change affects

data.body: Wave tags are a derived graph attribute stored by hand: /tmp/claude-1001/restamp_api.py emits one ddflow update per task (886 then 779 updates in one restamp), and its pure-depth N disagrees with core.schedule.waves (glob-aware, used only by plancheck). Make depth (true dependency depth, counting only open prerequisites incl. inherited needs) and wave (glob-aware) first-class derived values from ItemGraph: ddflow list --wave N / --depth, a wave line in brief and status, JSON fields. Keep reading existing wave:N tags for compatibility, flag stale ones in doctor, and document that tags are no longer maintained by hand. Decide the one meaning of 'wave' with D-wave-semantics (accepted) and state it in the output. Retire the restamp scripts' role. Coordinate with DX-waves-status (open question).
data.title: Depth and wave as derived values: ddflow list --wave, a brief line, no hand-stamped wave:N tags

data.body: Candidate G (graph-internal.md): predict conflicts between tasks whose declared globs are disjoint but whose files import each other. Value looked MEDIUM-LOW because git handles textual merges and conflicts are mostly textual. Measure before building: over the merge history count merge conflicts and gate/CI breakages after a merge caused by a parallel item, check whether the two items' globs overlapped, and whether the import graph (1-2 hops) would have flagged the pair; report precision (false alarms per true catch). Go/no-go with numbers; a go files the build task, a no-go closes this.
data.title: Would import-graph conflict prediction have caught real merge conflicts that disjoint globs missed? Measure first

data.body: services/review.py split_diff / chunk_files cut the diff by file then hunk and pack by size only, so a file and its tests or direct importers land in different chunks and no reviewer sees the cluster; Bd2332f8f2a showed a missing chunk hides which files nobody reviewed. Group changed files into clusters (file + its tests + importers present in the diff) and pass importers/callers of changed symbols as read-only context (not as diff, budgeted). Must not worsen accuracy: gated by RV-replay-corpus (recall measured on past confirmed findings) and RV-split-cap (split-on-truncate); report recall and time before/after. Time per review is NOT linear in diff size (RV-scale-research: exponent 0.26-0.41, dominated by reasoning tokens), so the goal here is accuracy and fewer wasted chunks, not raw speed.
data.title: Review scope by impact: chunk by module cluster, feed importers as read-only context

data.body: Re-measure on the same machine and log size as the audit (2735 items, 1487 py files): ddflow tests selection (cold 5.6 s -> warm < 1 s), ddflow next/plan unchanged or faster, ItemGraph build < 50 ms, test selection recall >= 0.98 at <= 15% of tests on the replay, review recall unchanged (RV-replay-corpus), restamp scripts no longer needed. Report the table in docs/ddflow/research/graph-acceptance.md, close or file follow-ups for every number that missed. Not a dependency but measured alongside: B-perf-mcp-start (resident folded state), which dominates ddflow next.
data.title: Acceptance: measured before/after for the graph phase, nothing slower, nothing less accurate
